subject: Welcome! Your document checklist (C-005, Family reunion)
message:
Hi Yui,

welcome to Elbe Example Relocation! We've opened your case C-005 (Family reunion). Here is your document checklist (10 items):

- Passport (valid for the whole planned stay) and a copy of all used pages
  Why: The office checks who you are and that your passport stays valid.
- One recent biometric passport photo (35 x 45 mm)
  Why: It goes on your residence card.
- Residence permit application form (signed)
  Why: This is the actual application. We pre-fill it and you only sign.
- Proof that you registered your Hamburg address
  Why: Everyone who moves into a flat in Germany registers the address. The confirmation is usually asked for.
- Rental contract and the landlord's move-in confirmation
  Why: Shows where you live. The landlord's confirmation is also needed for the address registration.
- Proof of health insurance
  Why: Health insurance is required for everyone living in Germany.
- Certified translations of documents that are not in German or English
  Why: Offices usually only read German or English. A certified translator can help.
- Marriage certificate (with apostille or legalisation if needed)
  Why: Shows the family relationship.
- Copy of your partner's residence permit or passport
  Why: Shows your partner's right to live in Germany.
- Proof that the flat is big enough for the family
  Why: The office checks there is enough living space for everyone.

No need to send everything at once. Reply with scans or photos whenever you have them, and we'll tick them off. If something is hard to get, just tell us.

Please note: this checklist is illustrative and not legal advice. The immigration office decides what it needs in your case.

Best wishes,
the Elbe Example Relocation team (fictional agency, demo only)

  Why: The office checks who you are and that your passport stays valid.

  Why: Health insurance is required for everyone living in Germany.
- Copy of the entry visa you travelled on
  Why: Shows how you entered. (In this illustrative rule set, US and Japanese nationals apply after arriving, so they skip this.)
- Certified translations of documents that are not in German or English
  Why: Offices usually only read German or English. A certified translator can help.
- University admission letter
  Why: Shows the study place.
- Proof of funds (for example a blocked-account confirmation)
  Why: Shows you can cover living costs while studying.
- Proof of language skills for your course (German or English)
  Why: The university and the office check you can follow the course.

No need to send everything at once. Reply with scans or photos whenever you have them, and we'll tick them off. If something is hard to get, just tell us.
